summary: GLP-1 radar, 29 Sep 2026. EASD 2026 is running in Milan (28 Sep to 2 Oct), and most of the fresh GLP-1 news is coming from it. Several of these stories are at the best stage for us: news outlets and press releases have covered them, but few creators have explained them properly yet. The top three are: (1) the WashU study of 333,000 veterans on stopping GLP-1s and heart risk ("metabolic whiplash"), now running on local TV news sites across the US; (2) the Nordic safety study required by regulators, with 97,464 matched pairs, finding no link between semaglutide and pancreatic cancer (a myth-bust); (3) new pill data (orforglipron/Foundayo vs oral semaglutide in an indirect comparison, plus results across menopause stages). CagriSema vs tirzepatide (REIMAGINE 5), the GLP-1 vs CPAP sleep apnea review and the hair-loss question are rising, so they need a clear angle that corrects the headlines. The SELECT '~20% of the heart benefit explained by weight loss' story has now appeared in 6 snapshots and is flattening; use it as an evergreen pillar anchor. Rejected: GLP-1 'microdosing' in perimenopause (violates our guardrails). Mark as caution: vision-loss (NAION) lawsuits, the brown fat mouse study, retatrutide (gray-market risk) and creatine.

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to higher heart attack, stroke and death risk: 'metabolic whiplash' in 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes (WashU)
candidates.angle: Why GLP-1 benefits depend on continuity. The effect goes beyond the scale: blood pressure, cholesterol and inflammation also come back. Frame it as 'plan any change with your prescriber', never 'don't stop'. It's an observational study in veterans with T2D, so say 'linked to'. Numbers to use: up to 22% higher risk after about 2 years off; an 18% risk reduction with continuous use vs 12% for people who restarted.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: The press release went out around 20 Sep. Scripps/NBC local stations syndicated it on 29 Sep and Nautilus covered it. 'What happens when I stop' is one of the biggest questions our audience asks, and YouTube has few careful explainers on it.

evidence.signal: 333,000+ veterans with T2D followed for 3 years; risk up to 22% higher after 2 years off
Science press pickup
Mainstream syndication across dozens of local stations on 29 Sep
'Whiplash' framing, 18% vs 12% risk reduction

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer: regulator-mandated Nordic registry study (97,464 matched pairs, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Myth-bust with a concrete number: '97,464 matched pairs across 3 countries, and no higher risk'. Be clear on scope: adults with T2D, semaglutide compared with insulin, sulfonylureas or SGLT2 inhibitors. Disclose that Novo funded it and that it was presented at EASD, not yet a full paper as of September. Bring in the global cohort on pancreatitis from J Pers Med as supporting evidence.
candidates.why_now: Medscape and Medical Xpress covered it on 28 Sep during EASD. It answers a common fear with reassuring, well-sized data, and hardly any creators have covered it yet.

evidence.signal: 97,464 matched pairs; Denmark, Sweden, Norway registries; EASD 2026
Regulator-mandated post-authorization safety study
Global propensity-matched cohort: GLP-1 RAs not associated with pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D
Semaglutide and pancreatic cancer risk in randomized trials

candidates.topic: Pill vs pill: orforglipron (Foundayo) vs oral semaglutide 25 mg in type 2 diabetes, a Lilly indirect comparison at EASD
candidates.angle: 'Which GLP-1 pill?' explained honestly. It's an indirect comparison (ACHIEVE-3 vs PIONEER PLUS), not a head-to-head trial, and Lilly funded it. Gaps at 52 weeks: 1.5 percentage points more weight loss and 0.3 points more A1C reduction. Pair it with Novo's analysis that points the other way in obesity. Don't give dosing advice; say the 25 mg oral semaglutide dose isn't US-approved for T2D (status as of Sept 2026).
candidates.why_now: The press release went out on 29 Sep at 07:00 GMT and investor and finance media picked it up. Searches for the two pills are growing, and a 'what an indirect comparison can and can't tell you' angle stands out.

evidence.signal: 1.5% greater weight loss, 0.3% greater A1C drop at 52 weeks (ITC, ACHIEVE-3 vs PIONEER PLUS)
Counter-analysis: how oral Wegovy outperforms Foundayo in obesity
Population-adjusted ITC: oral semaglutide 25 mg vs orforglipron 36 mg in obesity
Consumer explainer demand: Wegovy pill vs Foundayo

candidates.topic: GLP-1 pill orforglipron led to similar weight loss before, during and after menopause (post hoc ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: For women who worry 'menopause means it won't work for me': in these trials, weight loss beat placebo at every stage. Add the limitations: it's a post hoc analysis with small subgroups (10–225 women), and results came from 72-week trials. Tie in protein and strength training for muscle and bone after menopause.
candidates.why_now: Medscape, Medical Xpress, News-Medical and HCPLive covered it on 26–28 Sep, alongside Everyday Health's 'Can GLP-1s benefit women in menopause?'. Menopause content performs strongly (it appeared in our earlier snapshots too).

evidence.signal: Presented at EASD 2026 (Ciudin Mihai, Vall d'Hebron)
Similar weight loss across 3 menopausal stages
Up to ~14% body weight reduction by stage

candidates.topic: CagriSema beat tirzepatide in REIMAGINE 5, but it was a lower dose vs a lower dose in type 2 diabetes (12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss at 60 weeks)
candidates.angle: 'What the headline left out': both arms used lower doses, not the maximum. A1C results were similar (−1.71 vs −1.67 points), meeting non-inferiority. The trial was in adults with T2D on metformin and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor, and results are topline only (Novo announcement 21 Sep). Also explain what amylin adds to GLP-1.
candidates.why_now: It's running across finance and pharmacy media (Pharmacy Times 28 Sep, NewsNation, Yahoo Finance), and people are searching whether Novo has beaten Lilly. A clear explainer of the fine print is missing.

evidence.signal: Topline: 12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss at week 60
Trial in adults with T2D
HbA1c −1.71 vs −1.67, non-inferiority

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and sleep apnea: they cut breathing events by about 6–22 per hour, and CPAP by about 31 (JAMA Otolaryngology review)
candidates.angle: 'Helps, doesn't replace'. Tirzepatide is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity (SURMOUNT-OSA), and the review shows it can work alongside CPAP. Don't tell anyone to drop their CPAP; talk to your sleep doctor.
candidates.why_now: The Hill story on 28 Sep was syndicated to many Nexstar stations, alongside Yahoo's 'Should you take a GLP-1 for OSA?'. Good fit with our benefits-beyond-weight pillar.

evidence.signal: 6–22 fewer events/hour with GLP-1 vs ~31 with CPAP
Wide local-news spread

candidates.topic: Does GLP-1 cause hair loss? Modest link, low absolute risk (BMJ July 2026; NYU study on men predisposed to baldness, Sept 2026)
candidates.angle: A calm myth-bust. Much of the shedding looks like the temporary kind that follows rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium). Give the relative vs absolute risk. Cover what helps: enough protein, avoiding very low calorie intake, and asking your clinician to check iron and other nutrients. No supplement promises.
keywords: does wegovy make your hair fall out
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (28 Sep) and Times of India (28 Sep) are running explainers after the NYU study (16 Sep). This is a high-volume, recurring search, and a careful evidence-based take can rank.

evidence.signal: Hair loss can be more than temporary for some men
BMJ study: modest increased risk
GLP-1 therapies and hair loss, implications for counseling

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation, Eur Heart J), plus who lost the most in SELECT (Diabetes Care)
candidates.angle: 'Your heart may benefit even if the scale moves slowly'. Always name the population: adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes. Use it as an evergreen anchor for the benefits-beyond-weight pillar, updated with the 29 Sep Medical Daily coverage.
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 6 snapshots with momentum flat around 72. News-Medical (28 Sep) and Medical Daily (29 Sep) are still covering it. The mediation plus predictors pairing is a differentiated angle.

evidence.signal: SELECT mediation analysis
Predictors of peak weight loss in SELECT

candidates.topic: Why some people lose less on GLP-1: response varies widely (response categories in >10,000-patient matched cohorts; SELECT predictors of weight loss)
candidates.angle: 'Lower response isn't failure'. Explain the high, moderate, late and minimal response groups, what's linked to bigger losses, and that weight is one measure among many (heart, blood sugar). Bring questions to your prescriber, with no switching or dosing advice.
keywords: why am I not losing weight on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: DongA Science (27 Sep) reported limited effect in up to 15% of patients, and the Diabetes Care SELECT predictors paper came out 24 Sep. 'Ozempic not working' is a persistent search.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss dynamics with tirzepatide vs semaglutide, response categories
Predictors of peak body weight loss in SELECT
Systematic review: placebo-subtracted loss up to ~15% semaglutide, ~19% tirzepatide

candidates.topic: GLP-1 stigma: users hide treatment from friends and family, fearing the 'easy way out' label (Health Communication, 34 interviews, FSU)
candidates.angle: Compassionate myth-bust: obesity is a chronic disease, and medicine isn't cheating. Cover the 'weight bias paradox' and tips for talking about it. Qualitative study with 34 adults, so no percentages. Fits our integrity and compassion mission.
keywords: should I tell people I'm on wegovy
candidates.why_now: FSU release on 24 Sep, then Newsweek, Yahoo and Medical Xpress on 28 Sep. Highly shareable and relatable, and creators haven't taken it on.

evidence.signal: Mainstream pickup 28 Sep
34 adults aged 21–73, Health Communication

candidates.topic: Keeping weight off with fewer shots: Viking's experimental maintenance data (every-other-week/monthly dosing kept ≥90% of lost weight, early results, 180 adults)
candidates.angle: 'The next frontier is maintenance, not bigger losses'. Early-stage and investigational, and not available. Link it to the stopping-GLP-1 story and to what current evidence says about keeping results (habits, protein, strength training). Never point to research-peptide sources.
candidates.why_now: NewsNation (29 Sep) and NBC ('fewer injections') are covering it, and our audience's worry about regaining weight is a big driver.

evidence.signal: ≥90% of weight loss maintained with every-other-week dosing, 180 adults
Industry push for less frequent injections

candidates.topic: Retatrutide, the 'triple G': what the phase 3 T2D trial showed (TRANSCEND-T2D-1, The Lancet: up to −1.94 A1C points, 16.8% weight loss at 40 weeks) and why gray-market vials are dangerous
candidates.angle: 'What's coming, and why waiting matters'. It's investigational and not approved (as of Sept 2026). Explain what the triple mechanism means. Point to regulators' warnings about unregistered retatrutide vials, and stay firm on no research-chemical sources.
candidates.why_now: EASD opened with retatrutide diabetes data (Medical Daily, 28 Sep), Lilly's CEO pitched it as the next growth driver (29 Sep), and the Philippines FDA issued warnings about unregistered vials. Search interest is high and competition is rising.

evidence.signal: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 phase 3, 537 adults with T2D
Phase 3 T2D topline
A1C and weight results detail

candidates.topic: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss? New Clinical Nutrition paper, and what actually protects muscle on GLP-1
candidates.angle: Strongest evidence first: enough protein plus resistance training. Creatine is only a hypothesis in GLP-1 users (trial data are thin). Include the muscle share of weight lost in STEP/SURMOUNT body-composition substudies. Ties into our 'protein and muscle' double-down pillar.
keywords: how to keep muscle on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: The Clin Nutr paper (21 Sep) came out alongside Nutritional Outlook on the supplement industry's GLP-1 push (28 Sep). Creators will soon push creatine for GLP-1 users, so an evidence-first take gets in early.

evidence.signal: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss
Real-world 6-month tirzepatide body composition

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and sudden vision loss (NAION): lawsuits vs what regulators say
candidates.angle: A calm, factual explainer. European regulators list NAION as a very rare side effect of semaglutide. Cover what's known about causation (unproven, observational signals), which symptoms need urgent care, and to talk to your prescriber. No fear-mongering and no legal promotion.
candidates.why_now: MassLive and Boston.com lawsuit stories (26–28 Sep) and a Medical Daily piece on US labels (29 Sep). Anxiety-driven searches are rising, and a balanced voice is rare.

evidence.signal: FDA flagged signal in 2025; US labels lack NAION warning

candidates.topic: Zepbound/Mounjaro and brown fat: calorie-burning effect seen only in obese mice
candidates.angle: Mouse-to-human myth-bust. Headlines say 'burns calories', but the main human mechanism is still appetite and fullness. Show where this sits on the evidence ladder.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 snapshots, with coverage from ScienceDaily, AOL, Men's Journal and Health and Me on 26–28 Sep. Overstated headlines give a myth-bust something to correct.

evidence.signal: Press release: mouse study

candidates.topic: The GLP-1 pill race: Novo licenses Hengrui's oral GLP-1/GIP pill (HRS-1596), and where every pill stands
candidates.angle: A pipeline roundup: approved pills (oral semaglutide/Wegovy pill, Foundayo, depending on the region) vs investigational ones, with every status date-hedged. Explain why pills matter (no needles, access).
candidates.why_now: Reuters, GlobeNewswire and FirstWord covered the deal on 29 Sep, together with the Everyday Health oral-GLP-1 myths piece. Interest in pills is growing steadily.

evidence.signal: Novo licenses experimental GLP-1 pill from Hengrui

candidates.angle: Hook on the trend (CBS: chains adding GLP-1 menus), then deliver our guidance: protein first, fiber, eat slowly, hydrate, and ease nausea with smaller, less greasy meals. Evergreen life-on-GLP-1 pillar.
